chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the traveler who prays behind the resident, and he said: 'He prays two rak'ahs and proceeds wherever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler praying behind a resident in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of the traveler's prayer (*qasr*) when joining a resident (*muqim*), emphasizing that the traveler's obligation is limited to two rak'ahs regardless of the imam's duration. This ruling underscores the practical ease (*rukhsah*) granted to travelers in Shia jurisprudence, allowing them to conclude their shortened prayer and depart without being tethered to the resident's full four-rak'ah sequence. It highlights the distinct legal status of the *musafir* who prays behind a *muqim*, a scenario frequently discussed in the chapters on travel prayers.
